mathematics.assertion_tested: On the stated static spherical positive-field branch of the displayed HPI-Delta ADM action, the explicit weak expansion and independent variations give exact exponential AQUAL and no slip; the resulting isolated point-mass exterior admits the branch-correct W_-1 two-clock inverse, paired (a0,M) estimators, clock/curvature identities, a pointwise O(e^4) cross-radius null, and an exact all-orders branch-aware eccentric null on a bounded numerical window.
mathematics.coefficient_domain: Exact SymPy expressions over positive real symbols where possible; adaptive mpmath arithmetic for the Lambert endpoint inversion; deterministic IEEE-754 binary64 SciPy DOP853 integrations and bracketed scalar roots for bounded nonlinear-orbit audits; exact eccentric quadrature evaluated only on y_peri in [1e-6,25], e in [0.01,0.7], with inverse scans on y_peri in [1e-5,20] and an empirical 1e-8 q endpoint-resolution guard.
mathematics.conventions: epsilon=c^-2; N=exp(epsilon Phi); h_ij=exp(-2 epsilon Psi) delta_ij; g=Phi'>0; the local fixed-a0 scaling is Lambda=epsilon^2 Lambda_2; rho is rest-mass density; q=kappa^2/Omega^2 in the circular limit; q_e=(Omega_r/Omega_phi)^2=(2pi/Theta)^2 at finite eccentricity; r0 is the fixed-angular-momentum circular guiding radius; e=(r_a-r_p)/(r_a+r_p); R=(r_a+r_p)/2.

bounds.action_reduction: Symmetry-reduced static zero-shift branch; fixed-boundary finite-radius integrations by parts; fixed-a0 Lambda=epsilon^2 Lambda_2 scaling; not an unrestricted full-action Dirac proof.
bounds.circular_inverse: Positive-field point-mass exterior y>0 and 1<q<2; inputs must retain enough precision not to round q to an endpoint.
bounds.finite_e: Smooth analytic stable central potential and fixed angular momentum. The O(e^4) remainder is pointwise for finite y>0, and uniform only on compact y intervals away from inverse endpoints. The implementation guard is 0<=e<=0.03, matching the tested amplitude range; it is not a universal remainder theorem. Endpoint intervals require a caller-supplied absolute q-model error bound.
bounds.exact_finite_e: The displayed all-orders quadrature holds for y_peri>0 and 0<e<1. The double-precision forward implementation is audited only for y_peri in [1e-6,25], e in [0.01,0.7], and the inverse for y_peri in [1e-5,20]. The inverse enumerates sign-changing roots on a 32-cell log grid but does not certify absence of even-multiplicity or subgrid roots; nonzero residuals within 1e-8 in q of a finite search endpoint are explicitly unresolved. The guard exceeds four times the worst discrepancy in a 64-point comparison to the independent prior evaluator but is not a global error theorem.
bounds.orbit_solver: GM=a0=1; implicit force root solved at every evaluation; DOP853 rtol=2e-12, atol=2e-14, maximum step one circular period/120 for finite-e audit.
bounds.conditioning: Numerical minimum only over ln y in [-12,12], compared with a 4001-point grid.

residual_risks: The parent HPI-Delta action is independently dead at a smooth force-free center and lacks full acceptable PPN/cosmology closure.
The finite-e formula is asymptotic; the executable e<=0.03 guard matches the audited amplitudes but is not a rigorous uniform remainder theorem.
The exact eccentric inverse enumerates sign-changing branches only on a finite 32-cell log-y scan; global injectivity and absence of tangential/subgrid roots remain unproved.
The exact quadrature formula controls 0<e<1 and y>0 analytically, but the current double-precision executable deliberately rejects y_peri<1e-6, y_peri>25, e<0.01, and e>0.7.
The observables still need a 1PN map from chart radius/time to measured radii and periods for precision use.
External fields, extended source mass slopes, nonsphericity, tides, and multiple bodies can spoil the null.
A bounded literature search can miss equivalent formulas written in different notation.
